definitions.gloss: light brown sugar; sanontou (a Japanese sugar with a caramel-like color and flavor)
definitions.explanation: A Japanese type of brown sugar produced by repeatedly heating the sugar syrup that remains after white sugar is extracted. It is pale brown with a mild caramel flavor and is used widely in home cooking, especially for simmered dishes.

examples.japanese: {砂糖|さとう}は{三温糖|さんおんとう}を{使|つか}う。
examples.english: I use sanontou (light brown sugar) as my sugar.

examples.japanese: {三温糖|さんおんとう}を{入|い}れると{煮物|にもの}にコクが{出|で}る。
examples.english: Adding sanontou gives simmered dishes a richer flavor.

examples.japanese: うちの{家|いえ}では{白砂糖|しろざとう}より{三温糖|さんおんとう}を{使|つか}うことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: At our house we use sanontou more often than white sugar.

notes:
Written with {三|さん} (three), {温|おん} (warm, heat), and {糖|とう} (sugar). The name reflects the production process, in which the sugar syrup is heated three times, giving the sugar its characteristic caramel color and flavor.

Despite its appearance, {三温糖|さんおんとう} is not truly unrefined sugar — it is refined white sugar whose remaining syrup has been caramelized by repeated heating. It is especially popular in traditional Japanese cooking for {煮物|にもの} (simmered dishes) and {照|て}り{焼|や}き.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三温糖|さんおんとう}を{使|つか}う: to use sanontou
- {三温糖|さんおんとう}を{加|くわ}える: to add sanontou
- {三温糖|さんおんとう}{大|おお}さじ1: one tablespoon of sanontou

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {白砂糖|しろざとう}: white sugar — the most common refined sugar
- {黒砂糖|こくざとう}: unrefined brown/black sugar — darker and stronger-flavored
- グラニュー{糖|とう}: granulated sugar — larger crystals, neutral flavor
- きび{砂糖|ざとう}: raw cane sugar — pale brown, less processed than sanontou
